Who is the head chef at Chez Rose?

[Bryn Williams] Bryn Williams (born 6 June 1977) is a chef originally from Denbigh, Wales. He was the head chef and sole proprietor of Odette's Restaurant, Primrose Hill, London. He is notable for his success in a competition to cook the fish course for the Queen's 80th birthday celebrations on the television programme Great British Menu as a sous-chef. He is now widely regarded as one of Wales' best chefs and one of Britain's new crop of "celebrity" chefs. In June 2015 he opened his bistro, Bryn@Porth Eirias, on the seashore in the north Wales town of Colwyn Bay.

[Chez Rose, London W1: ‘One of the dining highlights of 2026’ – restaurant review] Chez Rose offers a sort of hospitality that feels centuries old, but when done well, will never be old hat (https://www.theguardian.com/food/2026/aug/02/chez-rose-london-w1-grace-dent-restaurant-review)

The day-to-day cooking is in the hands of head chef Mark Catchpole , whose CV takes in Roganic, Attica and The Fat Duck. The menu is a single sheet with a pretty logo, then a list of temptations: wild mushroom persillade with preserved truffle; Orkney scallop with Café de Paris butter; Cornish cod with mussel sauce and samphire; Aylesbury duck breast with black figs; and a T-bone steak for two at £145.
Next up, a stuffed courgette flower; a dish almost every eatery in the south of France serves all summer long, with varying success. Suspend your tiny violins; I’ve eaten so many poor versions. Here at Chez Rose, it’s a whole new dish entirely, and utterly marvellous. How is this courgette flower so crisp and delicious, I marvel, prodding at the rich ricotta innards, and licking up puddles of sauce vierge . “A courgette flower is always delicious,” argues Charles, who, being French, is wounded I’d say otherwise. He forgets the various backstreet cafes from Nice to Juan-les-Pins where I’ve eaten the equivalent of old daffodil heads in Castrol GTX.
Chez Rose 5 Pollen St, London. W1S 1NE, 020 7870 3730, chezroselondon.com. Open all week, lunch: noon–2.30pm (3.30pm Sun), dinner: 5.30pm (6.30pm Sun)–9.15pm (last seating). About £90 a head a la carte (Sunday lunch £49 for two courses, £59 for three), all plus drinks and service.

The head chef at Chez Rose is Mark Catchpole. 

FINAL: Mark Catchpole
